channel.title: The New Yorker — Reporting
channel.description: Latest reporting from The New Yorker

item.title: Can American Socialism Survive Its Success?
item.description: The movement has often seen its ideas flourish as its organizations withered. Will today’s resurgence follow the same course?

item.title: Jesse Eisenberg Can’t Help Overthinking It
item.description: His new film, “The Debut,” which stars Julianne Moore as a housewife turned egomaniacal actress, puts self-invented drama center stage.

item.title: The Buddhist A.I. Sect That Wants to Take Over Silicon Valley
item.description: MAPLEpromises to teach us how to live in the age of A.I. Its secret mission is much stranger.

item.title: Venezuela’s Collaborator-in-Chief
item.description: Delcy Rodríguez and the new American imperialism.

item.title: Would You Dissect a Human Body?
item.description: A doctor visits a lab where yoga teachers and massage therapists cut into cadavers.

item.title: After a Record Loss, Leopold Aschenbrenner Is Still Betting Everything on A.I.
item.description: “Next year is the last year that anything in modern life still feels a little normal,” Aschenbrenner, an investor and an A.I. prophet, says.

item.title: The Kings of Cocaine Are Masters of Stealth
item.description: Primeiro Comando da Capital, a gang so organized that it has its own constitution, favors quiet profit over public terror.

item.title: Is Norway’s Oil Fund a Blessing or a Curse?
item.description: In a culture used to thrifty living, a two-trillion-dollar bonanza makes people very uneasy.

item.title: Scott Bessent’s Economic Turnaround
item.description: The Treasury Secretary made a fortune as a money manager for George Soros. Can he stabilize the U.S. economy under Donald Trump?

item.title: The Great Wealth Transfer Is Causing Trust Issues
item.description: As baby boomers get ready to pass on their trillions, messy inheritance battles are on the rise.
